subject: Regional data lifecycle playbook for Marketplace listing (AWS/GCP/Azure) - Q&A
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@cloudbridge.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudBridge Partnerships <partners@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing - regional data lifecycle questions

Hi Grace / Ben,

Thanks for picking up the Marketplace listing — our compliance team sent over a short set of questions focused on how Redwood will handle region-specific retention and deletion for customers who procure via CloudBridge Marketplace (we run customers in US, EU, and APAC accounts across AWS/GCP/Azure). Key asks:

- Can Redwood pin customer data to a specific cloud region (e.g., us-west-2 / europe-west1 / asia-southeast1) when the customer is onboarded via Marketplace?
- What is the standard retention policy and is it configurable per-customer?
- For deprovisioning initiated from the Marketplace (cancellation or marketplace revocation), what is the deletion SLA (fully scrub backups, snapshots, and logs)?
- How are cross-cloud backups/replication handled (if at all) and can we guarantee no replication outside the chosen region?
- What evidence can Redwood provide for audit (deletion receipts, immutable logs, SOC2 artifacts)?

I attached a short list of questions (CloudBridge_Eval_Qs.pdf). Could we get a short response or proposal by EOD Friday? If it's easier, happy to take a 30-min technical call.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
CloudBridge

(Attachment: CloudBridge_Eval_Qs.pdf)

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing - regional data lifecycle questions

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (solutions) and Neha (security/compliance) to address the technical & audit bits; Marissa — bringing you in for marketplace-specific contract language.

High level answers up front:
- Yes, we support per-customer region pinning across AWS/GCP/Azure for Marketplace-provisioned accounts. That includes compute placement and primary object storage location.
- Retention is configurable per-account; defaults are set per-marketplace plan but can be shortened/lengthened via the onboarding contract and config.
- Deletion post-deprovision: we operate a staged deletion (tombstone -> scrub -> snapshot purge). We can commit to a contractual timeline (examples below) and provide deletion receipts/logs.
- Cross-cloud replication: we do not replicate primary customer data across clouds unless the customer explicitly requests multi-cloud redundancy. Backups/snapshots are subject to the same region constraints.
- Audit evidence: SOC2 report, immutable deletion logs, and KMS key rotation history are available under NDA; Neha will outline what we can include in a Marketplace listing.

I attached our one-pager for the data lifecycle. Proposed next steps: 1) quick 30-min call Wed/Thu to run through the edge cases, 2) follow-up with a short playbook and proposed SLA language for the Marketplace listing.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: redwood-data-lifecycle-onepager.pdf)

Thanks Grace — this is helpful. Two follow-ups from our compliance engineer:

1) Deletion SLA: our procurement team prefers a hard contractual commitment (e.g., full data purge including snapshots and backups within 30 days of marketplace-initiated termination). Can Redwood commit to that, and what are the exact steps you take to ensure snapshots and immutable backups are removed?

2) Metadata retention: will any customer metadata (billing ids, provisioning timestamps, audit events) remain after purge? We sometimes need minimal metadata for billing/chargeback reconciliation but it must be pseudonymized and flagged.

3) Logs & proofs: what form do deletion receipts take? Do you provide an immutable hash or signed log for audit purposes?

4) Cross-cloud check: if the customer onboards via AWS marketplace but opts for GCP compute later, how does Redwood prevent cross-cloud copy of staged artifacts?

I've attached a sample set of provider-side residency constraints (s3-residency-requirements.xlsx) to show what our customers typically ask for. Can Neha or Ben run through these and provide concrete wording we can put in the Marketplace listing by early next week?

Appreciate it — if a call is easier, we can book Thu morning.

—Priya

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing - regional data lifecycle questions

Hi Priya — thanks for the detailed follow-ups. Below are concrete responses so you can surface contract language in the Marketplace listing. Happy to discuss on a call if helpful.

1) Deletion SLA (Marketplace-initiated termination)
- Stage 1 (0-48 hours): account deprovisioned; primary data marked tombstoned. Active endpoints and API keys disabled immediately.
- Stage 2 (48 hours – 14 days): background scrub job removes ephemeral caches, prefixes, and token KV entries. Snapshots scheduled for destruction; we start snapshot deletion workflows.
- Stage 3 (14 – 30 days): final pass to purge object storage snapshots and overwrite blocks where supported; KMS key material associated with the account is scheduled for rotation and/or scheduled deletion per contract.
- Contract proposal: full purge of primary data and snapshots within 30 days; immutable audit logs available within 5 business days after purge completes.

2) Metadata retention
- By default we retain a minimal customer record for billing/operational reconciliation (customer id, provisioning timestamp) for 12 months, pseudonymized where requested.
- If CloudBridge needs zero-retention, we can include a zero-metadata option as a Marketplace tier; this will require a short onboarding checklist and may affect dispute resolution/billing reconciliation.

3) Deletion receipts & audit evidence
- We provide a signed deletion receipt containing: deletion job id, timestamps for each stage, list of storage objects removed, and a SHA256 digest for the deletion summary. Deletion receipts are stored in an append-only store; access can be provided to auditors on a time-limited basis under NDA.
- SOC2 report and summary redacted control mappings are available; we can include a short compliance appendix in the Marketplace listing.

4) Cross-cloud replication & staged artifacts
- Redwood does NOT copy primary customer data to a different cloud provider unless explicitly configured during onboarding.
- If a customer later requests multi-cloud compute, we perform an explicit data transfer with documented consent and log the transfer in the immutable audit trail; transfers are on-record and cannot be performed silently.

Recommended Marketplace listing language (short form):
"Redwood Inference supports per-customer region pinning across AWS, GCP, and Azure. Primary customer data and backups will remain in the chosen region unless the customer explicitly requests multi-region or multi-cloud redundancy. For Marketplace-initiated terminations, Redwood will complete a full purge of primary data and associated snapshots within 30 days and provide a signed deletion receipt for audit"

Links & artifacts we can share after an NDA: SOC2 summary (link), deletion-receipt-schema (link), and our internal residency runbook (redwood-residency-runbook-v1.docx).

If this aligns, Grace / Marissa — can you pull this into a short playbook and proposed SLA paragraph for the Marketplace listing? Priya — if CloudBridge has specific contract wording you prefer, send it over and we'll map it.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer, Compliance
Redwood Inference
